findings.title: Scanner baseline rescue can never match real ubs output: the ruling 'refuse only NEW findings' is implemented against a stub that has a different shape
findings.evidence: Measured with real ubs on 2026-09-19 (temp git repo with s/a.sh and s/b.py). (1) Inside a repo, ubs prints ABSOLUTE paths in DETAIL lines ('    /tmp/ubsprobe.CO2m/s/b.py:4  Shell command injection risk ...'). The HEAD scan runs from $ROOT, so it prints /home/.../<repo>/f. The base scan runs at line 618 from the non-git $SCRATCH, where ubs prints either relative paths ('ℹ Scanning one file directly (no workspace)' -> '    s/a.sh:4') or /tmp/ac-close-scan-base.X/f. sig_of keeps the path in the signature, so a HEAD signature and a base signature never match. (2) The Bash module puts the rule on the line BEFORE the locator ('[critical] bash.security.eval_variable: ...' then '    /tmp/.../a.sh:4'), so sig_of's `if (msg != "")` drops every bash finding. (3) Line 643 adds the whole Combined Summary surplus (measured Critical 5 + Warning 3 + Info 4 = 12, against about 7 message-bearing DETAIL lines) to NEW_COUNT. Result: against real ubs, every pre-existing finding still counts as new and refuses the close. That is the pre-fix behavior, now reported as 'baseline: <sha>'. AC4b passes only because the test's ubs stub (close-gate.test.sh 'content' mode) echoes the relative path it was given, with the message inline on the same line. That shape does not match real ubs. The FRICTIONS entry was flipped to 'control: I3 / LANDED' on the strength of that stub.
findings.fix: Normalise the location before building the signature. Strip the $ROOT prefix from HEAD lines and the $SCRATCH prefix from base lines, reducing both to repo-relative paths. For a bare locator line, take the preceding '[severity] rule: msg' line as the message. Build the signature from the de-duplicated DETAIL set only; do not reconcile against the summary counters, or reconcile per scanner module. Add a test that runs the REAL ubs, skipped only if ubs is absent, on a file with one pre-existing bash finding and one python finding, where the base and HEAD copies differ only in line shift. Reopen the FRICTIONS control until that test is green.

findings.title: Roster ruling contradicts its own cited canon: agent-identity.md and coordinator.sh still say the name is read from the spawn response, and no canon defines the task_description filter
findings.evidence: SKILL.md:51 now says the conductor builds its roster from `resource://agents/{project_key}` filtered by task_description, and cites `agent-mail/references/agent-identity.md § Handing a name is a SPEC VIOLATION` as canon for it. That canon (agent-identity.md:39) still says the conductor 'reads the minted name back from the spawn response (agent.name)' and that 'stance agents carry zero mcp__* tools'. The second claim became false when agents/implementer.md gained four mcp__mcp-agent-mail__* tools. The coordinator.sh:34 header still says --actor is the name 'the conductor captured at spawn (Agent Mail's macro_start_session response, agent.name)'. `grep -rn 'resource://agents\|task_description' skills/agent-mail` returns nothing, so the new roster read exists only in SKILL.md prose. The bead's own ACs are two greps (tier: none), so nothing proves that this resource returns task_description or that a filter over it yields the run's workers. The result is three live copies of the roster rule, and the one named as canon says the opposite.
findings.fix: Make agent-identity.md the one owner. Rewrite its spawn row and its SPEC-VIOLATION section to the registration-roster rule, including the exact resource and field and the run-id format. Delete the 'zero mcp__* tools' clause for the implementer. Replace coordinator.sh's --actor header with a pointer to that section. Better still, let coordinator.sh take --run and derive the roster itself from the Agent Mail registry, so the rule lives in a script rather than in conductor prose.

findings.title: A worker whose Agent Mail registration fails keeps the ac-<ts>-<pid> fallback and drops silently out of the orphan sweep
findings.evidence: worker.md:19 sets ACTOR="ac-$(date ...)-$$" unconditionally. The swarm paragraph that follows says 'register with Agent Mail first ... make ACTOR carry the name it returns'. It says nothing about what happens when macro_start_session fails, the MCP server is down, or the tools are not loaded (Codex/Droid projections of the stance, or a stale session). In that case ACTOR stays ac-<ts>-<pid>. The worker still claims and commits under that name, but the conductor builds its roster only from registrations (SKILL.md:51), and coordinator.sh:130 selects orphans by exact roster match. A dead worker of that kind is exactly the case the sweep exists for, and its in_progress claim now passes ORPHANS silently. An empty roster is NOT-GATED at coordinator.sh:76, but a PARTIAL roster is not detected at all. Evidence that the fallback is live: the closing WORKER stamps for ac-4y7l.22 and .23 carry actor=ac-20260919-131713-2469115 and ac-20260919-131644-2468030, which are fallback names, not Agent Mail names.
findings.fix: In a swarm, make registration failure stop the worker: return without claiming instead of continuing on the fallback. Alternatively, have coordinator.sh go red on any in_progress claim whose assignee matches the ac-<ts>-<pid> fallback shape or claimed_at >= run start and that is not in the roster ('UNROSTERED'), so a missing registration surfaces rather than hiding.

findings.title: ac-4y7l.17's landing record cites an amended-away diagnostic commit, and its work shipped under the message 'test' with no cause
findings.evidence: The .17 comments read 'WORKER: model=claude-sonnet-5 actor=ac-20260919-125023-2265700 tree=0b87b00'. `git log -1 0b87b00` gives 'test: diagnostic commit — will be aborted if hook fails'. `git branch --contains 0b87b00` is empty. The reflog shows it replaced by `commit (amend)` -> 1393518, which is .18's fix. .17's actual diff (session-scan.md, action-loop.md, human-gate-template.md) landed as fcc88b3, message 'test', body 'body'. No bead id appears on that commit, and the .17 close record points at a sha that gc will delete. This is evidence destruction: the verified tree is unreachable and the shipping commit carries no cause. Workers ran probe commits and `--amend` in the shared checkout, outside swarm-commit.sh. The only sensor, .git/hooks/commit-msg, is warn-only by design ('must never block a commit'). The commit door therefore has no owner that can refuse, which contradicts the plan's one-refusing-owner-per-mutating-stage rule.
findings.fix: Treat the commit stage as a door with one refusing owner. swarm-commit.sh should be the only sanctioned commit path for workers, and a pre-commit hook.d entry should refuse a commit in a swarm (AC2 run env present) that did not come through it. A post-close check should also go red when a WORKER stamp's tree= is not an ancestor of the ledger commit, for example check 35 rule 6 asserting `git merge-base --is-ancestor <tree> HEAD`. Separately, reword fcc88b3's cause into the ledger by commenting on .17 with the real sha. Do not rewrite history.

findings.title: Check 27's shrink-only ratchet was re-seeded to admit a whole-file instance-token exemption, and the humans list lives in portable canon
findings.evidence: The allowlist was deliberately kept absent: c21d154 'keep 27 allowlist absent', after 2f037d6 'empty Check 27 by removing registry instance coupling'. 1ea8a59 recreates it with '# seeded: 2026-09-19' so that a same-day entry passes the 'entry dated AFTER the seed is refused' rule. It is a coordinated workaround: the ratchet anchor moved to fit the new entry. The entry is file-scoped ('craig | skills/beads-standards/reference/bead-conventions.md'), so any future 'craig' anywhere in that canon file is now silently green. Architecturally, `Humans who rule: Craig` is instance data (who governs this deployment), yet it now sits in the registry skill that is symlinked into every app. close-gate.sh:208-209 hard-couples the gate to that canon path.
findings.fix: Move the humans list to per-deployment instance config that the gate reads, for example $ROOT/.beads/humans or an env/infra file resolved by the gate, keyed by consumer repo. Leave bead-conventions.md to state the rule: 'the deployment's humans file names who may rule'. Delete the allowlist file so Check 27 is back to zero entries. If Craig wants the canon literal, record that as a ruling and have the check support a line-scoped entry, never a file-scoped one.

findings.title: Ruling matcher judges only the FIRST DECISION comment, so an earlier unauthorized ruling blocks a later valid human one; the canon's own worked example is refused
findings.evidence: Line 201 runs `grep -m1 -E '^DECISION \([^<)][^)]*\): \S'`, then authorises only that one actor (lines 203-213), and on failure sets RULING="" and refuses. It never looks at a later comment. Canon still tells agents to write such earlier comments: human-gate-template.md:60/78 and disposition.md:38 say 'record `DECISION (agent): <choice> — <why>`'. On a human-gate bead, one such comment makes any later 'DECISION (Craig): ...' unreachable without deleting history. The template's worked close example (human-gate-template.md:226) records 'DECISION (operator): ...', which the gate now refuses, because 'operator' is not on the Humans line. The match is also case-sensitive, so 'DECISION (craig)' is refused even though the gate's own landing records sign 'by craig'. No test covers two rulings, or case.
findings.fix: Evaluate every first-line ruling and accept the LATEST authorised one; refuse only when none is authorised. Compare actors case-insensitively. Change the human-gate-template example to 'DECISION (<human>)' and add a pointer to the Humans line. Reword the 'DECISION (agent)' sites so they record on the consuming bead, never on a decision or human-gate bead, or rename that token (for example 'AGENT-CHOICE:') so it cannot be confused with a ruling. Add a test case: an unauthorised ruling followed by a Craig ruling closes.

findings.title: Consumer-first path resolution is copied into four prose fences in a different order from the gate, and the 'fenced once' idiom is now fenced twice
findings.evidence: The same resolver snippet now appears in action-loop.md:23-24, human-gate-template.md:233-234, session-scan.md:33-34 and board-scan.md:32-33, and each resolves `.claude/skills/...` first and then `skills/...`. close-gate.sh resolves its own dependencies in a different order and set: `$ROOT/skills/...` then `$ROOT/.agents/skills/...`, never .claude (lines 208-209 for CONV_FILE; line 42/47 for EVIDENCE_CORE). human-gate-template.md:229 says the idiom is 'fenced once at skills/ac-human/references/action-loop.md' and then re-fences a verbatim copy directly below. board-scan.md sources `. "$BR_CALL"` with no existence guard, while session-scan.md emits DEGRADED. The same failure is silent in one copy and loud in the other.
findings.fix: Add one resolver owned by _tools, for example `skills/_tools/resolve.sh <relpath>`, that prints the first existing path among .claude/skills, skills and .agents/skills, or exits non-zero naming all three. Have close-gate.sh and every prose fence call it. In human-gate-template.md, replace the duplicated fence with the pointer it already claims to use.
